name: Decisions and architecture only
text: Record architecture, design decisions, constraints, and the reasons behind them. Skip small implementation details, variable names, and step-by-step edits unless they change how the project works.

name: Skip transient status
text: Ignore transient status: test runs, build output, retries, progress reports, and intermediate attempts that were replaced. Only record what is still true after the conversation ends.

name: User-facing behaviour
text: Focus on how the product behaves for its users: features, settings, defaults, workflows, error messages, and limits. Phrase entries from the user's point of view.

name: Strict next steps
text: Only create next steps the user asked for or clearly agreed to. Record the assistant's own suggestions as questions, not next steps. Mark a next step done (supersede it with a fact) only when the events show it was finished.

name: Bugs, causes, and fixes
text: Record each bug that was found: its symptom, root cause, the fix, and any test that now covers it. Note known bugs that are still open as next steps.

name: Security and privacy
text: Pay special attention to security and privacy: secrets handling, authentication, permissions, data that leaves the machine, and risky defaults. Never copy a secret value, key, token, or password into an entry; describe where it lives instead.

name: Onboarding a new developer
text: Write for a developer joining the project next week: how to build, test, and run it, how the code is laid out, conventions to follow, and pitfalls that cost time. Prefer durable facts over history.

name: Fewer, broader entries
text: Prefer a few broad entries over many narrow ones. Merge related details into one entry, and when new events refine an existing entry, supersede it with an updated version instead of adding a near-duplicate. At most 8 entries per batch.

name: Concise
text: Keep every entry short: a title under eight words and a body of one or two plain sentences.

name: Rationale first
text: For every decision, record why it was made and what alternatives were rejected, as stated in the events. A decision without a recorded reason gets lower confidence.

name: Capture open questions
text: Capture unresolved questions and disagreements explicitly as questions, including who needs to answer them when the events say so. Do not resolve them yourself.

name: Release notes
text: Treat the wiki like running release notes: record each shipped change as a fact titled by what changed, with why it changed and anything users must do differently.

name: Careful confidence
text: Be conservative with confidence. Use 90 or more only when the user stated something directly or the events show it settled. Assistant claims that the user never confirmed stay below 70.

name: Code is the source of truth
text: Treat the source files as the final word. Call an entry supported only when the code directly shows it; documentation or newer memories alone are not enough for supported.

name: Judge substance, not wording
text: Judge whether the substance of the entry still holds. Ignore wording, naming, and small details that changed without changing the meaning.

name: Newer decisions win
text: When a newer decision or fact replaces or reverses the entry, call it contradicted even if old code still matches the entry.

name: Is this next step done?
text: For next steps and questions, decide whether the work was done or the question answered. Done or answered means contradicted (the entry is no longer open); still open means supported.

name: Check file references
text: Check every file, path, function, and setting the entry names. If one no longer exists in the supplied excerpts, say so and call the entry contradicted unless it is clearly renamed.

name: Sceptical reviewer
text: Be sceptical. Prefer unclear over supported when the evidence only partly covers the entry, and keep confidence below 80 unless the evidence is direct.
